## 8b7d1307ff93

**Classification: reproduced semantic shortcut plus independent lint defect.** Generator SHA-256 `0ca419e3a698490603a5b281aa0c2af2f4d371942951f7ae36605d98dd53ed1a`; canonical rule hash `9f70bbc3da17`.

The intended rule repeatedly fills any 2×2 window containing three copies of one nonzero color and one zero until closure. The generator, however, samples a distinct color for every L and rejects origins that are close in both coordinates. An isolated L becomes one solid 2×2 block, and that block alone cannot trigger further growth. Thus the plausible shortcut **“fill only the corners licensed by the original input once”** fits every ordinary generated sample even though the summary advertises cascading iteration.

A source-bound finite probe generated 300 ordinary grids—seeds 0–99 at sample index 0 for each difficulty. All 300 passed `self_check`; the one-pass rival agreed with iterative closure on all 300. Evidence: `checks/audit/8b7d1307ff93/distribution.json` and `distribution-command.log`.

The exact counterexample in `checks/audit/8b7d1307ff93/input.json` uses two separate same-color L-trominoes whose missing corner is shared. It passes the target validator at medium/default difficulty. It is outside the documented generated domain because the Ls share a color and are close; that exclusion is precisely why the generator cannot teach iteration. One-pass filling adds only the shared center. The Racket fixed point grows the upper-left 3×3 square, additionally filling row 0/column 2 and row 2/column 0. Evidence: `checks/audit/8b7d1307ff93/racket.json` and `comparison.json`.

The focused lint stage also reproduces a missing required `RULE_HASH` and two non-probed singleton axes (`position_bias`, `density`): `checks/audit/8b7d1307ff93/lint-run/checks/8b7d1307ff93_before_lint.log`. This audit target was not edited.
